1.note: The term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.
Zechariah is using the word translated as **And** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

2.note: The phrase **Thus says Yahweh of Armies** introduces a direct quotation from Yahweh. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

2.q: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת קִנֵּ֥אתִי לְ⁠צִיּ֖וֹן
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. In this verse, Zechariah is quoting what Yahweh says directly. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh of hosts, am passionate for Zion]

2.q: קִנֵּ֥אתִי לְ⁠צִיּ֖וֹן קִנְאָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וְ⁠חֵמָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה קִנֵּ֥אתִי לָֽ⁠הּ
2.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [I have been extremely jealous for Zion with great heat]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **jealousy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and desire to keep her as my own]
The pronoun **her** refers to Zion. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [for Zion with]

Yahweh is speaking of his strong jealousy as if it were **heat**. If this image communicates well in your language, please use it. If not, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I have been jealous for her with much anger toward her enemies]

3.note: The phrase **Thus says Yahweh** introduces a direct quotation from Yahweh. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. In this verse, Zechariah is quoting what Yahweh says directly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will return to Zion]

The expression **Jerusalem will be called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people will call Jerusalem]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh of Armies**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [and my mountain]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **city of faithfulness** that is characterized by being faithful. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the faithful city]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [where people are faithful]

Yahweh assumes that readers will know that **the mountain of Yahweh of hosts** refers to Mount Zion. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and Mount Zion]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Armies will be called “the mountain of]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **the mountain of holiness** as a mountain that is characterized by holiness. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the holy mountain]

4.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:2.

Yahweh is referring to all elderly people by naming two major components, **Old men** and **old women**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [The elderly]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [and each person with a staff in hand]

Yahweh is using **from a multitude of days** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of old age.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because of old age]

5.note: The expression **will be filled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Boys and girls will fill the open areas of the city,]

Yahweh is referring to all children by naming both major components, **boys** and **girls**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all the children]

6.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:2.

Yahweh is speaking as if this were a hypothetical possibility, but he means that it is actually true. If your language does not state something as a condition if it is certain or true, or if your readers might think that what Yahweh is saying is uncertain, then you could translate this as a confident statement. Alternate translation: [Since it is wonderful]

Yahweh is using **in the eyes of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in the judgment of” or “in the opinion of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in the opinion of the remnant of this people]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that nothing is too difficult for him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [it will not be wonderful in my eyes]
The phrase **declaration of Yahweh of Armies** affirms that the preceding words are from Yahweh. In your translation, use a natural way of representing this kind of affirmation in your language.

7.note: Yahweh is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Look!]

Yahweh is referring to all of the places where his people are scattered by naming two extremes, **the land of the sunrise** and **the land of the setting of the sun**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from every country, whether east or west]

8.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a covenant relationship in which he is the God whom the people worship and serve. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [I will be the God whom they worship and serve]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I will be** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize his own commitment to be the God of his people, matching the reciprocal relationship he describes: they will be his people, and he himself will be their God. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [and I myself will be]

The phrase **in faithfulness and in righteousness** expresses a single idea. The word **faithfulness** tells more about **righteousness**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [with faithful righteousness]

9.note: Yahweh is using **hands** to represent the whole person and their courage to work. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Be strong and courageous]

9.q: הַ⁠שֹּֽׁמְעִים֙ בַּ⁠יָּמִ֣ים הָ⁠אֵ֔לֶּה אֵ֖ת הַ⁠דְּבָרִ֣ים הָ⁠אֵ֑לֶּה מִ⁠פִּי֙ הַ⁠נְּבִיאִ֔ים אֲ֠שֶׁר בְּ⁠י֞וֹם יֻסַּ֨ד בֵּית־יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת
9.note: This could mean: (1) the message Zechariah is giving today is almost the same as the message that Haggai (probably) gave when the temple construction started. Alternate translation: [you who are hearing today these same words as were from the mouth of the prophets who stood there on the day the house of Yahweh of Armies was founded] (2) prophets had repeatedly given a similar message ever since temple construction had started, these people had been hearing that. Alternate translation: [you who have kept hearing in these days these words from the mouth of the prophets ever since the day the house of Yahweh of Armies was founded]

The expression **was founded** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they founded the house of Yahweh of Armies]

The expression **to be built** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [so that they would build the temple]

Yahweh is using **the mouth of the prophets** to represent what the prophets said. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the prophets]

10.q: כִּ֗י לִ⁠פְנֵי֙ הַ⁠יָּמִ֣ים הָ⁠הֵ֔ם שְׂכַ֤ר הָֽ⁠אָדָם֙ לֹ֣א נִֽהְיָ֔ה וּ⁠שְׂכַ֥ר הַ⁠בְּהֵמָ֖ה אֵינֶ֑⁠נָּה וְ⁠לַ⁠יּוֹצֵ֨א וְ⁠לַ⁠בָּ֤א אֵין־שָׁלוֹם֙ מִן־הַ⁠צָּ֔ר וַ⁠אֲשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־כָּל־הָ⁠אָדָ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ בְּ⁠רֵעֵֽ⁠הוּ
10.note: Here Yahweh is providing background information to help his listeners understand the contrast he is making. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

Yahweh is using the expression **to the face of** to mean “before” or “previous to.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [before those days]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [the wages of people]

10.q: שְׂכַ֤ר הָֽ⁠אָדָם֙ לֹ֣א נִֽהְיָ֔ה וּ⁠שְׂכַ֥ר הַ⁠בְּהֵמָ֖ה אֵינֶ֑⁠נָּה
10.note: Yahweh is referring to all sources of income by naming two major components, **the wages of man** and **the wages of the beast**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [no money could be made in any way]

Yahweh is referring to all of a person’s daily activities by naming two opposites, **the one going out** and **the one coming in**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And for everyone in all their activities]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [safety]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [every person against their neighbor]

11.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:6.

11.q: וְ⁠עַתָּ֗ה לֹ֣א כַ⁠יָּמִ֤ים הָ⁠רִֽאשֹׁנִים֙ אֲנִ֔י לִ⁠שְׁאֵרִ֖ית הָ⁠עָ֣ם הַ⁠זֶּ֑ה נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת
11.note: Yahweh uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between the former days and the present time. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [However, now I will not treat the remnant of this people as I did in the former days’—the declaration of Yahweh of Armies.]

12.note: Yahweh is speaking of future prosperity as if it were a **seed** planted in peace that would produce an abundant harvest. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [there will be peace and prosperity]

Here the word **For** introduces not a reason but an explanation. You may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [Instead]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:10.

Yahweh speaks of **the vine**, **the land**, and **the heavens** as if they were persons who could **give** things to people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [fruit will come from the vine, produce will come from the land, and dew will fall from the heavens]

13.q: וְ⁠הָיָ֡ה כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁר֩ הֱיִיתֶ֨ם קְלָלָ֜ה בַּ⁠גּוֹיִ֗ם בֵּ֤ית יְהוּדָה֙ וּ⁠בֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֵּ֚ן אוֹשִׁ֣יעַ אֶתְ⁠כֶ֔ם וִ⁠הְיִיתֶ֖ם בְּרָכָ֑ה אַל־תִּירָ֖אוּ תֶּחֱזַ֥קְנָה יְדֵי⁠כֶֽם
13.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **you were a curse in the nations** was certainly true, so it will certainly be true that Yahweh will save them and they will be a blessing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Just as it was certainly true that you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so it will certainly also be true that I save you and you will be a blessing. Do not fear; let your hands be strong!]

Yahweh is speaking of his people as if they were a **curse**, meaning that other nations would refer to them as an example of what it means to be cursed. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the other nations used you as an example of what it means to be cursed]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of a **curse**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [of people who were cursed]

Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **house of Judah** figuratively means all the people descended from the patriarch Judah, and **house of Israel** means all the people descended from the patriarch Jacob, who was also known as Israel. Alternate translation: [people of Judah and people of Israel]

Yahweh is speaking of his people as if they would actually become a **blessing**, meaning that other nations would refer to them as an example of what it means to be blessed. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you will be an example of what it means to be blessed]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of a **blessing**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [you will be blessed]

Yahweh is using **hands** to represent the whole person and their courage to work. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Be strong and courageous]

14.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **harm**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to harm you]

Yahweh uses the words **Just as** and “thus” (next verse) here to indicate a contrast between what he did in the past and what he will do in the future. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language.

The phrase **says Yahweh of Armies** is a parenthetical remark that reminds the listener that these are Yahweh’s words. In your translation, use a natural way of representing this kind of attribution in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this phrase explicitly.

15.note: The words **I have turned** and **I plan** express a single idea. The word **turned** indicates that Yahweh is planning again, reversing his earlier purpose to bring harm. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [I again plan] or [I have decided once more]

16.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **truth**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what is true]

Here the masculine term **his** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [every person with their neighbor]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and peaceful resolutions]

Yahweh is using **gates** to represent the places where legal judgments are made. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in your courts]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [judge in your gates faithfully and peacefully]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **judgement**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and make decisions that bring peace]

17.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [do harmful things]

Here the **heart** represents where a person’s thoughts and intentions exist. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in your thoughts]

The phrase **the declaration of Yahweh** affirms that the preceding words are from Yahweh. This quotation began at verse 2. In your translation, use a natural way of representing this kind of affirmation in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this phrase explicitly.

18.note: Zechariah is using the word translated as **And** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
See how you translated the similar expression in [8:1](ta:08).

19.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **joy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [joyful times]

The terms **joy** and **gladness** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [times of great joy]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **gladness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [when you gladly celebrate]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:16.
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:16.

21.note: Here, **the face of Yahweh** represents the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the presence of Yahweh]

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. For example, you could translate the direct quotation as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [saying that they should quickly go … And that they themselves would also go]

The speaker is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I also will go** already includes this meaning. The speaker is doing that to emphasize his own eagerness to join in seeking Yahweh. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I myself will also go]

22.q: לְ⁠בַקֵּ֛שׁ אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת & וּ⁠לְ⁠חַלּ֖וֹת אֶת־פְּנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה
22.note: See how you translated these same phrases in the previous verse.

23.note: Yahweh is making an extreme statement, saying **ten men from every language of the nations**, to emphasize the great number of foreigners who will seek to worship him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the emphasis in a different way. Alternate translation: [countless people from every language and nation]

To **grab the hem** of someone’s robe was a symbolic action that expressed a strong desire to accompany that person. If this would not be understood in your culture, you could use a comparable symbolic action from your culture or describe what this action meant. Alternate translation: [will beg, they will beg to come along with]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **will grab** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [will grab tightly the hem of]

23.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֗ר נֵֽלְכָה֙ עִמָּ⁠כֶ֔ם כִּ֥י שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ אֱלֹהִ֥ים עִמָּ⁠כֶֽם
23.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. For example, you could translate the direct quotation as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [saying that they want to go with him because they have heard that God is with him]
